clue.text: Sure wobbly as belly out!

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and out of shape, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation of certainty about a paunch hanging loose over a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic agreements: 'Sure!' and 'Absolutely!' are interchangeable replies of total assent.

clue.text: Area coming up in murder case

indicators.note: coming up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something that surfaced during a murder investigation.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word; it is the signal that the letters lie within 'murder case', so it is added as the hidden-word indicator. In a down clue 'coming up' reads them bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of land measurement equal to 4,840 square yards, so it names an area.

clue.text: Smile more fake, as wine waiter

indicators.note: a fake smile is put on rather than real, and here the letters are rearranged into something false

explanation.surface: Advice to a wine waiter to put on a bigger false grin for the customers.
explanation.definitionFit: The restaurant steward who advises on and serves the wines is known by this French title.

clue.text: Drink at bedtime, perhaps? About time!

indicators.note: about means going round, so the late hour surrounds the time letter

parts.note: bedtime is one example of a late hour, hence the 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a nightcap and adds an impatient 'About time!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as an exclamation, but 'About' puts LATE around T.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky espresso coffee is a kind of hot drink served in cafés.

clue.text: In play, pair reinterpreted clip art

indicators.note: in says the rearranged pair goes inside the word for play

parts.note: to toy with something is to play with it

indicators.note: something reinterpreted is given a new reading, so the letters of pair are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A theatre production where two actors give a fresh reading of some clip-art images.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedges and shrubs clipped into ornamental shapes are a gardener's art made by clipping, so 'clip art' is a witty description.

clue.text: Characters, those renting rooms?

definitions.meaning: ... of the alphabet are written characters
people who let rooms out to tenants are ... in a whimsical sense

explanation.surface: A cast of characters described as a group of landlords.
explanation.definitionFit: Alphabet symbols are characters; and one who lets property is, playfully, a 'letter', so the plural covers landlords.

clue.text: Old man greedy, taking every other bit

indicators.note: every other bit means taking alternate letters from the two words, starting from the second

explanation.surface: An elderly man who is grasping, taking a share of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old has lived or existed a long time; 'aged' is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Inexperienced politician

definitions.meaning: a ... recruit is new and untried
a member of an environmentalist party, such as the ... Party, is a politician

explanation.surface: A dismissive description of a novice in government.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word means raw and untried, and also names a member of an ecology party.

clue.text: Unhappiness of knight in place for camp dancing?

indicators.note: in says the knight's letter goes inside the run of the other two pieces

parts.note: disco is a style of dancing
a tent is a place for camping out
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight is miserable at being stuck in a nightclub for flamboyant dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place for camp dancing' tempts as one phrase for a nightclub, but 'camp' belongs with 'place for', and 'dancing' is read separately; the knight sits between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Discontent is dissatisfaction, a state of being unhappy with one's lot.

clue.text: Page covering right agreement

indicators.note: covering means the word for page wraps around the letter for right

parts.note: to page someone is to call or contact them

explanation.surface: A single page of a contract that sets out a right.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a binding deal between parties, a formal agreement.

clue.text: Area of responsibility turning the clock back?

indicators.note: back, as in turning a clock back, says the word for the clock is read from its end

parts.note: a timer is a clock that is set turning or running to count time

explanation.surface: Putting the clocks back is presented as someone's job.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface phrase 'turning the clock back' carries the reversal: TIMER read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the scope of a person's duties, the field they are responsible for.

clue.text: Transpose in mix-up that could result in woman signing sponsorship deal

indicators.note: a mix-up jumbles things, so the letters of the first word are scrambled

explanation.surface: Swapping something round in a muddle could leave a woman signing up as a sponsor.
explanation.definitionFit: A patroness is a female patron, a woman who gives financial backing to an artist or cause.

clue.text: Always in container, English drink

indicators.note: in says the word for always goes inside the container

parts.note: a bag is a container
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A flask always carrying an English drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water, a formal word for something to drink.

clue.text: Dance beat has vitality

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
go means energy or vitality, as in 'full of go'

explanation.surface: A dance whose rhythm is full of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine ballroom dance in two-four time is one example of a dance.

clue.text: Relative pace beginning to slow, tries shifting

parts.note: a step is a pace

indicators.note: beginning to means only the first letter of the following word is taken
shifting means the letters of tries are moved around

explanation.surface: A relative whose pace starts to flag keeps making efforts to move.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter of one's step-parent is a relation by marriage, so a relative.

clue.text: Dry sherry initially quaffed by two rugby union teams?

indicators.note: quaffed by means swallowed by, so the number takes the letter inside it

parts.note: a rugby union side has fifteen players, so two sides make thirty

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of sherry is used

explanation.surface: Two rugby teams downing dry sherry, which hardly fits the after-match picture.
explanation.walkthrough: A rugby union team has fifteen players, so two teams make THIRTY; S goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dry in the sense of needing a drink means wanting liquid, parched.

clue.text: Foreign article held by small beams

indicators.note: held by means the foreign article is enclosed by the word for small

parts.note: slight means small, as in a slight chance
un is the French indefinite article, meaning 'a'

explanation.surface: An imported item kept by a minor figure who smiles broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' looks like a verb (smiles), but it is the noun: rays of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from the sun arrives as rays or beams, so beams stand for sunshine.

clue.text: Excited as leant closer?

definitions.note: something that closes up a gap or joint, a noun for a material that seals

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who got thrilled as they leant in nearer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer' reads as 'nearer', but it means a thing that closes: a filler for cracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealant fills and shuts gaps, so it is cryptically a thing that closes them.

clue.text: Last word on capitalism's ending in hollow reform

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the first piece comes before the rest

parts.note: amen is said at the end of a prayer, the final word

indicators.note: in says the final letter goes inside the hollow

parts.note: a dent is a hollow or depression

indicators.note: ending means only the final letter of capitalism is taken

explanation.surface: A final verdict on the demise of capitalism within a superficial reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' looks like an adjective describing 'reform', but it is the noun DENT; M goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change made to improve a law or text, a form of reform.

clue.text: Root cut, average previously

indicators.note: previously means the word for average comes before the word for cut

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
a snip is a small cut

explanation.surface: A garden vegetable trimmed back, having been of middling quality before.
explanation.definitionFit: This pale tapering vegetable is eaten for its root, a root vegetable.

clue.text: Worker in ceramics nailing one more up the wall?

indicators.note: nailing means catching and holding, so the worker encloses the letter for one

parts.note: a potter makes ceramics
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A craftsman hammering a plate onto a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the wall' is British slang for crazy, as is 'potty', so the comparative means crazier.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up the wall is to be mad, and potty is a synonym, so more potty is more crazed.

clue.text: Bird that's cold facing north

parts.note: a bitter wind is a bitingly cold one

explanation.surface: A bird facing a freezing northern wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A bittern is a wading bird of the heron family known for its booming call.

clue.text: Risk securing limp cover

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the word for risk wraps round the word for limp

parts.note: a bet is a risk taken on an outcome
lank means limp and lifeless, as of hair

explanation.surface: An insurance-style wager that fastens down a feeble policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed covering is a blanket; the noun means something that covers.

clue.text: Foreign national occasionally fiery on a quiz show

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters are used, the second and fourth of fiery

parts.note: QI is a British television quiz show hosted first by Stephen Fry

explanation.surface: A foreign contestant who sometimes gets heated on a television quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: QI is a long-running BBC panel quiz show.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of a Middle Eastern country is a national of a foreign state.

clue.text: A price to pay for coral?

definitions.note: a ring of coral forming an island, the question mark flagging an example

parts.note: a toll is a charge paid for passage on a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Asking what someone would charge for a piece of coral.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring-shaped reef enclosing a lagoon is formed of coral, so coral defines it by example.

clue.text: A tailless feline in toy box

indicators.note: in says the shortened feline with A goes inside the toy

parts.note: a teddy bear is a child's toy

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a cat is a feline

explanation.surface: A cat without a tail found inside a toy chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'box' is the definition, not a container indicator: the item is a small tin for storing leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A small tin or casket for storing loose leaves for brewing is a kind of box.

clue.text: Lost on a ship

definitions.meaning: aboard a vessel, sailing on the ocean

explanation.surface: Someone missing aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means bewildered and also literally afloat on the ocean.

clue.text: Lower part to bring up

definitions.meaning: the back or bottom, the hind portion of something

explanation.surface: Instructions about a bottom section that has to be lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the back or behind; the verb means to raise children.

clue.text: Not clever enough to bag first in physics? That's fine

definitions.note: a thin, fine object, described as a thing that is fine

indicators.note: to bag is to capture, so the phrase encloses the letter

parts.note: too thick means too stupid, insufficiently clever

indicators.note: first in means the opening letter of physics

explanation.surface: Someone too dim to get a top mark in physics, who shrugs it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's fine' reads as acceptance, but it means 'that which is thin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny slender stick for cleaning teeth is a very thin object, so fine in the slim sense.

clue.text: Kid was vacillating, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: swayed means wavered, was vacillating

explanation.surface: A child who could not make up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child, but it is leather from young goats, often napped.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid leather and napped suede are both soft leathers, so one stands for the other.

clue.text: Embraced by hero, legendary part

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside these words, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A famous character taken on by a legendary actor.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's part in a play is the character they play, also called a role.

clue.text: Measuring instrument for farm machinery

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a tractor is a piece of farm machinery

explanation.surface: A device for measuring designed for agricultural vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircular instrument used to measure angles in geometry is a measuring tool.
